column1: Minimum Size Subarray Sum — given an array of POSITIVE integers `nums` and a positive integer `target`, return the minimal length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is ≥ target. Return 0 if none exists. Example: target=7, nums=[2,3,1,2,4,3] → 2 (subarray [4,3]).
column2: PATTERN: Variable-size sliding window. | INSIGHT: Expand right; while sum is valid, shrink left and record length. | STEPS: 1) l=0, total=0, ans=inf. 2) For r in range(n): total+=nums[r]; while total>=target: ans=min(ans, r-l+1); total-=nums[l]; l+=1. 3) Return 0 if ans==inf else ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Sliding window assumes positive values — for any-sign use prefix sum + monotonic deque.

column1: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters — given a string `s`, return the LENGTH of the longest substring with no repeated characters. Example: s='abcabcbb' → 3 ('abc'); s='bbbbb' → 1; s='pwwkew' → 3 ('wke').
column2: PATTERN: Sliding window + last-seen hashmap. | INSIGHT: When we see a repeat inside the window, jump l to last_seen[c]+1 (but never backwards). | STEPS: 1) last={}, l=0, ans=0. 2) For r,c in enumerate(s): if c in last and last[c]>=l: l=last[c]+1; last[c]=r; ans=max(ans, r-l+1). | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(min(n, charset)). | PITFALL: The l=max(l, last[c]+1) check is essential — stale entries outside the window must be ignored.

column1: Substring with Concatenation of All Words — given a string `s` and a list `words` of equal-length strings, return all starting indices in s where SOME permutation of words appears as a contiguous concatenation (no chars between words). Example: s='barfoothefoobarman', words=['foo','bar'] → [0,9].
column2: PATTERN: Fixed-size word-chunk sliding window, run word_len times. | INSIGHT: All words have the same length, so a window of word_len*num_words bytes can be slid by word_len. Run the scan from word_len different starting offsets to cover all alignments. | STEPS: 1) need = Counter(words). 2) For offset in range(word_len): l=offset, have={}, count=0; slide r by word_len, read word; if word not in need: reset; else have[word]+=1, count+=1; while have[word]>need[word]: drop left word; if count==len(words): record l; advance l. | TIME/SPACE: O(n·word_len) / O(num_words). | PITFALL: Forgetting the word_len starting offsets makes you miss valid windows.

column1: Minimum Window Substring — given strings `s` and `t`, return the SMALLEST substring of s that contains every char of t (counting multiplicities). Return '' if none. Example: s='ADOBECODEBANC', t='ABC' → 'BANC'.
column2: PATTERN: Sliding window with need/have counters and a "formed" tracker. | INSIGHT: Track how many UNIQUE chars are fully satisfied, not raw matches. Window is valid when formed == len(need). | STEPS: 1) need=Counter(t), have={}, formed=0, ans=(inf,0,0). 2) Expand r: have[c]+=1; if have[c]==need[c]: formed+=1. 3) While formed==len(need): record window; have[s[l]]-=1; if have[s[l]]<need[s[l]]: formed-=1; l+=1. 4) Return slice. | TIME/SPACE: O(n+m) / O(charset). | PITFALL: Compare have[c]==need[c] (exact) when incrementing formed, and have[c]<need[c] (strictly less) when decrementing.
